name: Turbo Hearts
description: Turbo Hearts is an American Hearts variant introduced at Upenn in the 1980s by Richard Garfield, based on the Chinese game Gong Zhu. Four players receive 13 cards each, pass three in rotation, then may turbo-charge one of four special cards (Ace of Hearts, Queen of Spades, Jack of Diamonds, Ten of Clubs) to multiply its effect. Lowest score when someone reaches 100 wins.

history.origins: Turbo Hearts was introduced at the University of Pennsylvania in the 1980s by Richard Garfield (later creator of Magic: The Gathering). It is an American variant of the Hearts family and an American version of the Chinese game Gong Zhu (Catch the Pig). The parent game Hearts emerged in the United States in the 1880s and descends from earlier trick-avoidance games such as Reversis.
timeline: 1980s: Introduced at University of Pennsylvania by Richard Garfield; American Hearts variant.

setup.dealing: All 52 cards dealt one at a time clockwise; each player receives 13. After the deal, each player passes three cards face-down in a rotating cycle: first hand pass left, second hand pass right, third hand pass across, fourth hand no pass, then repeat.

rules.objective: Avoid scoring penalty points. Hearts count 1 each, Queen of Spades 13; Jack of Diamonds is a bonus (minus 10). Whoever captures the Ten of Clubs doubles their score for that hand. After the pass, players may turbo-charge one of four special cards (Ace of Hearts, Queen of Spades, Jack of Diamonds, Ten of Clubs), which multiplies that card's effect. The player with the lowest total when someone reaches 100 wins.
rules.gameplay: Deal and pass as in standard Hearts: all 52 cards dealt one at a time (13 each); each player passes three cards in a rotating cycle (left, right, across, no pass). After the pass, each player may place one of the four special cards face up in front of them (turbo-charge). The holder of the 2 of clubs leads it to the first trick. Players must follow suit if possible; highest card of the suit led wins the trick. Hearts may not be led until a heart has been played to a previous trick (hearts broken) or the leader holds only hearts. A turbo-charged card may not be played the first time that suit is led. Turbo-charged Queen of Spades or Jack of Diamonds doubles that card's value; turbo-charged Ace of Hearts doubles all hearts for that hand; turbo-charged Ten of Clubs quadruples the hand score for the player who captures it. Shooting the moon: capture all penalty cards to deduct 26 from your score or add 26 to everyone else's.

scoring.description: Each heart 1 point, Queen of Spades 13; Jack of Diamonds minus 10 (bonus). Capturing the Ten of Clubs doubles the taker's hand score. Turbo-charged cards multiply values. Shooting the moon: 26 points from shooter or added to others.
scoring.winCondition: Lowest total score when any player reaches or exceeds 100.

synthesis.shortDescription: Hearts variant: faster play or different passing rules.
